---
title: Thesis to publication content plan
---

This plan guides editorial restructuring only. It does not change the completed
thesis, data, models, or reported results.

| Publication section | Primary thesis source | Initial editorial direction |
|---|---|---|
| Abstract | `analysis/thesis/_index.qmd` | Draft anew after the results and supplement boundary are settled. |
| Introduction | `analysis/thesis/introduction.qmd` | Condense broad background; foreground multiaged redwood silviculture, regeneration under retained overstory, and the need to jointly consider fuels. |
| Methods | `analysis/thesis/methods.qmd` | Retain the study design and measurements needed to interpret regeneration and fuels; move implementation detail to the supplement if it does not affect inference. |
| Regeneration results | `analysis/thesis/results.qmd` | Lead the results. Retain redwood and tanoak basal-area/density and sprout-height findings, subject to later presentation or modeling review. Retain other species descriptively where useful, but do not plan a dedicated Douglas-fir seedling analysis. |
| Fuel results | `analysis/thesis/results.qmd` | Report disaggregated pre- and post-PCT fuel conditions as reference values and retain the PCT-associated contrast as a central management result. Revisit component definitions, phase estimates, and uncertainty before finalizing treatment comparisons. |
| Discussion | `analysis/thesis/discussion.qmd` | Center silvicultural implications, then connect pre- and post-PCT fuel conditions to integrated fuels and fire management. Describe possible future applications without presuming a specific use. Remove repeated interpretation and unsupported certainty. |
| Tables and detailed models | `analysis/thesis/tables.qmd` | Keep only tables essential to the main narrative; move expanded model outputs, pairwise comparisons, and supporting summaries to a supplement. |

## Editorial guardrails

- Preserve citation keys unless a verified bibliographic correction is needed.
- Distinguish editorial revision from analytical revision in commit messages and
  the publication change log.
- Do not alter raw data or thesis-era generated objects.
- Do not present a new result until its publication-specific analysis and
  supporting figure or table have been reviewed.
